adequacy_assessment.readme_stated_purpose: convex-backend triggers, subscription/invalidation model (read-sets, SubscriptionManager, OCC validation), and candidate plug-in points for an incremental engine (index backfill, search index maintenance, subscription invalidation, OCC validation)
adequacy_assessment.triggers: Section 1 adequately covers what triggers mean in convex-backend context
adequacy_assessment.subscription_invalidation_model: Section 2 thoroughly covers read-sets, SubscriptionManager, and OCC validation with architecture and flow diagrams
adequacy_assessment.plug_in_points: Section 4 systematically identifies four plug-in points: index maintenance, search index maintenance, query execution/invalidation, and OCC validation
strengths: Clear architectural diagrams showing information flow
Concrete file paths and function names for all major components
Explicit comparison between what convex-backend does vs. does not have (incremental computation)
Systematic identification of plug-in points at natural abstraction boundaries
limitations: Citation error on lines 233-239 for core logic comment (should be 187-191)
Subscription invalidation flow uses high-level pseudocode rather than detailed source
Limited discussion of edge cases (e.g., log purging, subscription lifecycle during system shutdown)
No discussion of scalability limits or performance characteristics of interval overlap queries
QueryRemoved semantics and lifecycle details not covered in depth
adequacy_assessment.reasoning: Document adequately covers the README's stated purpose and provides sufficient foundation for the plans (1a/1b/1c/Direction 2) to understand convex-backend's reactivity model and identify plug-in points. However, one factual citation error and limited coverage of edge cases prevent a 'pass' verdict. The error is in documentation citation, not in the conceptual understanding.
